result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns the raw fetch Response when credential sharing is on. In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff changes to `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` — a fetch Response has no `.data` property, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError, exactly as the finding describes. This only triggers when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, but the mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: With credential sharing enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data (the googleauth response shape), so token is undefined and token.access_token throws a TypeError — and the sync response body is never read, so the shared token is never applied. On any deployment with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every Google Calendar token refresh crashes; the operation falls back to the expired token and Google Calendar availability/booking calls fail with auth errors until the app is reinstalled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` still assumes the refresh call returns an object with `.data` (Google client shape): `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` (lines added around the `refreshOAuthTokens` call). But `refreshOAuthTokens` (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, which does not have a `.data` property. That makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime. Additionally, the sync path never reads/decodes the response body (no `response.json()`), so even if it didn't crash, it wouldn't apply the shared token payload.
